messages:
alex: heads-up — saw a weird spike in token refresh calls from the mobile SDK during a rolling canary. App in background, single user action, but we got 5 refreshes.
maria: ugh that sounds like the auth retry loop we thought was solved. repro on which android/os?
alex: Pixel 7a, Android 14 beta, okhttp 4.11.0, retrofit 2.9.0. Happens when phone goes to background and network blips for ~300ms.
sam: what does the log show? stack or timing?
alex: pasted a trimmed log snippet below

```
I/OkHttp: Call canceled: okhttp3.RealCall
auth: refresh started token_id=abc123
I/OkHttp: Call queued: okhttp3.RealCall
auth: refresh started token_id=abc123
network: CONNECTED (wifi)
auth: refresh started token_id=abc123
```

alex: notice the Call canceled + queued sequence and simultaneous refresh starts.

erin: are you using synchronous token fetch or suspending/coroutines adapter?
alex: coroutines + retrofit CallAdapter, inside an interceptor we suspend to fetch token if 401.

maria: interceptor doing suspend inside intercept chain can cause dispatcher starvation if not careful. also background Doze could pause threads.
sam: hmm but multiple refreshes = interceptor is not deduping inflight refreshes. We tried an in-memory mutex before.

alex: we have a dedupe (mutex) but it relies on same Call instance key. OkHttp seems to create new call objects when connection resets -> parallel interceptor runs.

ci-bot: FYI: reproduced in CI with emulator android-14-api 34 image. Failing test: auth/retry/duplicate-refresh-001

erin: workaround idea: make token fetch idempotent and use a shared refresh-in-flight atomic reference keyed by account id (process-wide), not per-call.

maria: agreed — also consider switching to synchronous token refresh on a separate executor from OkHttp dispatcher to avoid nesting suspends inside interceptors.

sam: can we change our interceptor to return 503 on transient network and let call retry handle it instead of doing token fetch inline? might avoid multiple inflight refreshes.

alex: patch suggestion — move refresh to AuthManager.refreshTokenIfNeeded(account) that returns a Deferred<String> stored in a ConcurrentHashMap; await that in interceptor.

maria: that pattern worked for other SDKs. watch out for lifecycle though — app background + process kill will leave deferred unresolved? handle cancellations.

erin: quick snippet I used before:

```
val inflight = ConcurrentHashMap<String, Deferred<String>>()
fun refresh(accountId: String): Deferred<String> = inflight.computeIfAbsent(accountId) {
  GlobalScope.async(Dispatchers.IO) { doRefresh() }.also { d -> d.invokeOnCompletion { inflight.remove(accountId) } }
}
```

maria: GlobalScope = 😬 but ok for short lived retry. better to wire a lifecycle scope or dedicated single-thread executor for refresh.

alex: we'll try inflight map + IO dispatcher. planning to add integration test simulating brief connectivity blips.

sam: also add a test for okhttp cancel->new-call behavior: create flaky socket that closes after 200ms and assert single refresh.

alex: filing a small RFC and a test PR. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: linked failure: https://ci.internal/reports/1234 — reproducer + logs attached

maria: nice. can you also note specific okhttp version in the PR and include repro emulator command? others might have different behaviour on older okhttp.
alex: will do. PR incoming in ~1h.
